CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Bangkalan Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bangkalan.
3. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
4. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological, to the victim.
5. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
6. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
7. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or for certain purposes.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
10. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
12. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
13. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband-wife or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, as well as mother and her children.
15. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (a domestic helper, a driver, and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2 The principles of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. respect for the rights of victims.
b. justice and gender equality.
c. non-discrimination.
d. best interests of the victim.
Article 3 The objective of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence based on gender equality and the best interests of the child, for violence that occurs in the household and/or public.

CHAPTER III
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Article 4 (1) Every community or individual has the right to report incidents of violence against children and women.
(2) Every victim has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage, and confidential handling, provided by individuals, groups, or institutions, whether from the Regional Government or non-government.
Article 5 In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

CHAPTER VI
ASSISTANCE
Article 11
Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have expertise in the relevant field to provide counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have worked together with PPT.

REGENT OF BANGKALAN
DECIDES:
REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

CHAPTER V
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
Part One
Institutional
Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT forum.
(2) PPT Bangkalan may forward case referrals from sub-districts in Bangkalan.
(3) Provisions regarding PPT shall be further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Part Three
Principles of Service

Article 9
The provision of services to victims shall be carried out free of charge, promptly, safely, empathetically, without discrimination, easily accessible, and with a guarantee of confidentiality.

Article 10
PPT managers are obligated to provide services in accordance with the service principles as referred to in Article 9.

GOVERNMENT OF BANGKALAN REGENCY
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANGKALAN REGENCY

CHAPTER VIII
CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 13 This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.
In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Bangkalan Regency.
Enacted in Bangkalan on the date of 7 August 2009 •

5. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
6. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
7. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or for certain purposes.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
10. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
11. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in a Hospital, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
12. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
13. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband-wife or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, as well as mother and her children.
15. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (a domestic helper, a driver, and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

CHAPTER III
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Article 4 (1) Every community or individual has the right to report incidents of violence against children and women.
(2) Every victim has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage, and confidential handling, provided by individuals, groups, or institutions, whether from the Regional Government or non-government.
Article 5 In the event of violence, every victim has the right to obtain assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to obtain guarantees of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2 The principles of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. respect for the rights of victims.
b. justice and gender equality.
c. non-discrimination.
d. best interests of the victim.
Article 3 The objective of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence based on gender equality and the best interests of the child, for violence that occurs in the household and/or public.

CHAPTER V
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
Part One
Institutional
Article 7
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT forum.
(2) PPT Bangkalan may forward case referrals from sub-districts in Bangkalan.
(3) Provisions regarding PPT shall be further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Part Three
Principles of Service

Article 9
The provision of services to victims shall be carried out free of charge, promptly, safely, empathetically, without discrimination, easily accessible, and with a guarantee of confidentiality.

Article 10
PPT managers are obligated to provide services in accordance with the service principles as referred to in Article 9.
